subject: Animation
title: The Fox and the Hound: Generational Shift
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Fox and the Hound: Generational Shift.

hook.text: The Fox and the Hound in 1981 was the first Disney film made almost entirely by new young animators.

buildup.text: The old guard — the Nine Old Men — were retiring. A new generation had to prove themselves worthy.

discovery.text: Tim Burton, John Lasseter, and Brad Bird all worked at Disney during this period before leaving.

twist.text: The film's emotional story about lost friendship proved the new team could handle real dramatic weight.

climax.text: The Fox and the Hound was the bridge between Disney's past masters and its future renaissance leaders.

punchline.text: Disney's future legends cut their teeth on a story about a fox and a hound.

quiz.question: Why was The Fox and the Hound significant for Disney's studio history?
options: It was Disney's highest-grossing animated film
It was the first film made largely by new young animators as the Nine Old Men retired
It introduced computer animation to Disney
